plan_sequence.literal_excerpt:
5.5.3 Step 3: Use Battle Plans. The attacker may use any 
battle plans (7.5) they rule, once each. Then the defender 
may use any battle plans they rule, once each. The bandits 
use all battle plans they rule that have no cost.

empty_attack_pool.literal_excerpt:
If the attack pool would lose an attack die but it has none 
left, add a defense die to the defense pool.

bandit_eligibility.literal_excerpt:
The bandits 
use all battle plans they rule that have no cost.

plan_color_and_rule.literal_excerpt:
7.5 Battle Plans
Battle plans are Campaign modifiers (7.4) whose icon is 
surrounded by a crown and have different rules. Red, blue, 
and gradient power boxes indicate battle plans that can only 
be used by the attacker, defender, or either, respectively.
7.5.1 Added Use Limit. You can only use battle plans that 
you rule (not if your pawn is at their site but you do not rule it).

plan_cost.literal_excerpt:
7.1.2 Cost. To use a power, you must pay its cost, if any. 
Denizens, relics, and edifices have a cost on their braid. 
Sites and the Conspiracy have costs described in their text.

occupied_plan_once.literal_excerpt:
7.5.3 No Pay Limit. You can pay the cost for a battle plan 
that has favor or secrets on it. (You can still only use it once.)

once_per_campaign.literal_excerpt:
7.5.3. Pay Limit. 
The clarification says I can only use a battle plan “once.” What does that mean?
It means you cannot use the same battle plan multiple times in a single Campaign action.

defender_priority.literal_excerpt:
In rare situations where the defender and/or Allies disagree about timing, priority, or order of who can use a battle plan and when, the declared defender chooses the order. 
(For example, if two players want to use the same power, the declared defender chooses who gets to use the power. If a player might or might not choose to use Code of Honor, which would restrict other battle plans from being used, the declared defender can force them to say whether they are using Code of Honor or not before the declared defender chooses which battle plans they are using.)

ambiguity_reasoning: The primary rule makes no cost a property required of an eligible bandit plan: “plans they rule that have no cost.” It does not create a general exemption from paying the costs of every ruled plan.

The comma before “without cost” separates that phrase from the noun phrase “all plans at sites they rule.” The scenario result independently repeats this all-plans permission. Interpreting both as no-cost-plans-only would insert an unstated eligibility restriction into their applications, rather than merely complete an omitted general step.

The attached phrase “all ruled plans with no cost” naturally restricts the plan set, so its correct general rule is credited. Its coexistence with a broader explicit answer/application is an internal contradiction; the quote is not ignored, and it is not used to silently erase the broader claim.

No cost-bearing card or specific paid-plan use is invented as part of the supplied scenario. The contradiction is the entry’s stated general permission over all ruled plans, compared with the source’s expressly narrower permission.

“May” in the scenario result is not independently penalized: it is read alongside the answer and quote stating that bandits use all qualifying plans. The answer’s correct color restriction is also credited; color eligibility does not restore the missing cost eligibility.
